turns.question: Under Title 17, when must a person who acquires more than five percent of a class of registered equity securities file a Schedule 13D, and when may they file a Schedule 13G instead? Cite the sections.

report.markdown:
Under **17 CFR § 240.13d-1**, the filing obligations for beneficial owners of more than five percent of a class of registered equity securities are as follows:

### **When Schedule 13D must be filed (§ 240.13d‑1(a))**
Any person who, after acquiring beneficial ownership of an equity security of a class registered under Section 12 of the Exchange Act (or an insurance-company or closed-end-fund security specified in § 240.13d‑1(i)(1)), becomes the beneficial owner of **more than five percent of that class** must file a **Schedule 13D within five business days after the date of the acquisition** [1].

### **When Schedule 13G may be filed instead**
A person who would otherwise be required to file Schedule 13D may file the short-form **Schedule 13G** in two circumstances:

1. **Qualified institutional investors (§ 240.13d‑1(b)(1))**
   The person must:
   - have acquired the securities **in the ordinary course of business** and **not** with the purpose or effect of changing or influencing control of the issuer (or in connection with any transaction having that purpose/effect);
   - be one of the enumerated institutional types (broker‑dealer, bank, insurance company, registered investment company, registered investment adviser, ERISA/government employee benefit plan or endowment, parent holding company meeting the 1% test, savings association, church plan, non‑U.S. functional equivalent, or a group composed entirely of such persons);
   - have promptly notified any other person on whose behalf it holds discretionary securities exceeding 5% of the class.
   The initial Schedule 13G is due **within 45 days after the end of the calendar quarter** in which the obligation arose (or within five business days after the month-end if ownership exceeds 10% before quarter-end) [1].

2. **Other passive investors (§ 240.13d‑1(c))**
   Any person **not** covered by paragraph (b) may file Schedule 13G in lieu of Schedule 13D if:
   - the securities were **not acquired with the purpose or effect of changing or influencing control** of the issuer;
   - the person is **not** a paragraph (b) institutional reporter; and
   - the person is **not the beneficial owner of 20% or more of the class**.
   The filing deadline is **within five business days after the date of the acquisition** [1].

### **Key sections cited**
- **17 CFR § 240.13d‑1(a)** – General Schedule 13D filing trigger and 5‑business‑day deadline.
- **17 CFR § 240.13d‑1(b)** – Schedule 13G eligibility for qualified institutional investors (ordinary‑course, no control intent, specified entity types, notice requirement).
- **17 CFR § 240.13d‑1(c)** – Schedule 13G eligibility for other passive investors (no control intent, not a (b) institution, ownership below 20%).
- **17 CFR § 240.13d‑1(d)** – Schedule 13G for persons who become >5% owners but are exempt from § 13(d)(6) filing (45‑day quarter‑end deadline).

**Limitations:** The excerpts above are from the 2026‑08‑17 eCFR snapshot; confirm the current text before relying on it for compliance.
